title: Built a browser drift game with Claude: every run is one mountain corner (three.js, works on phones)
author: Tad-Games
selftext:
Play free in your browser: [https://tad-mmlogo.itch.io/touge-one-corner](https://tad-mmlogo.itch.io/touge-one-corner)



This is Touge One Corner, a small drift game where each run is a single corner on a Japanese mountain pass. You get scored on angle, line, speed and flow, then you can watch a TV-style replay of your run (that's what the clip is).



\*\*How it was made\*\*

\- Code: written with Claude (Claude Code). I'm a hobbyist, so my job was mostly deciding what the game should feel like, playtesting, and telling Claude what felt wrong.

\- Stack: plain JavaScript + three.js, no engine. Runs in the browser on phone or PC.

\- 3D car models: NOT AI-generated. They're CC BY models from Sketchfab, credited in the game.

\- The promo video was also recorded by a script Claude wrote (headless Chrome capturing the replay frame by frame).



\*\*What took the most time\*\*

\- Drift physics. Getting a slide that feels good but is still controllable with one finger took many rounds of "it spins too easily" / "now it grips too much".

\- The physics runs on a fixed timestep, so it behaves the same at 60Hz and 144Hz.

\- The replay system: trackside cameras, slow motion and a helicopter shot, directed automatically from the recorded run.



\*\*What I learned\*\*

\- AI is great at building systems fast, but the "feel" only gets good through lots of playtesting and very specific feedback.

\- Small scope helped a lot. "One corner" was easy to describe and easy to polish.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow!
